title: pfcp: correction of Outer Header IE bitshift

notes.body: I was wrong in !12191 . When "GTP-U/UDP/IPv4" is expected "N19 Indication" was set instead
Could we keep the array in increasing order?

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/13108/diffs?diff_id=837631749&start_sha=ee5ffa1d22245a377115c258b36f9857a910b66d#087fe683f643dcb0638caff602a2ad5cc9d71f2c_4492_4502)
Why do we have an extra space at the end of each string?
Can't remember why, but will be removed when change to bitmask handle

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/13108/diffs?diff_id=837631749&start_sha=ee5ffa1d22245a377115c258b36f9857a910b66d#087fe683f643dcb0638caff602a2ad5cc9d71f2c_4494_4502)
3GPP 29.244 describes this field as a bitmask, not an enum. IMHO we should display as such and not use proto_tree_add_item
Yeah, agree on this. will change to bitmask instead

Any reason for not combining both octets in a single proto_tree_add_bitmask_list() call? Would not it make more sense to display them as a single bitmask and not two separate ones?

Dividing them looked better, that was the reason. With divided octet it looks like this

![pfcp_one_oct](/uploads/781fdb030930a8cd838034ae1e7d5772/pfcp_one_oct.PNG)

with combine octet

![pfcp_two_oct](/uploads/fed5ef2e80084cd793690a78902ff999/pfcp_two_oct.PNG)

And keeping the increasing order as specified in 3gpp doc.
There is nothing preventing you from displaying using the bit order rather than the spec order. I find both displays disturbing.
haha, yeah it's disturbing

But this too doesn't look nice

![pfcp_two_oct_bitorder](/uploads/db9c736dbb769f416974a0126e4117a3/pfcp_two_oct_bitorder.PNG)

But maybe that is the best way to show this
This is what is sent over the wire. But if we do not add an hf entry for the bitmask, that's fine by me to display byte by byte. As you prefer.
But as the spec describes this field as being 2 bytes long, displaying it as such makes more sense to me.

changed this line in [version 6 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/13108/diffs?diff_id=839087144&start_sha=c4a7f1e5693f0d537cc9ba9a310d38eebac5c083#087fe683f643dcb0638caff602a2ad5cc9d71f2c_4520_4510)
Version 6 gives the output as the third ex above, I think that is the best representation of this weird list
Why not keep an hf entry for the bitmap itself?
proto_tree_add_bitmask_list doesn't take hf entry, that's why. Or did I missing something?

You could use proto_item_add_subtree() to create the subtree used in , butproto_tree_add_bitmask_list() maybe this is not required. I was wondering if people could be interested in doing a filtering based on the bitmap itself, but maybe it is useless.
Easier to filter on the boolean from the bitmask list, ex pfcp.pfcp_outer_hdr_desc.udp_ipv4 I would say
OK.
